Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph FEB OPINION NO. HON. MARILOU T. CLERIGO Vice-Mayor Municipality of San Ricardo Province of Southern Leyte Dear Vice-Mayor Clerigo: s. 204 This has reference to your letter dated 7 August 2018, requesting for this Department's opinion on the manner of filling-up the position in the Sangguniang Bayan of San Ricardo, Southern Leyte and the legality of the documents submitted by Mr. Zeromy Buba to assume as the 8th ranking Sangguniang Bayan Member,. Per your letter, in May 2016 elections, Mr. Buba run for mayoralty candidate as independent candidate but unfortunately, did not win. The following were declared by the Commission on Elections as duly elected officials of the Municipality of San Ricardo: Mayor: Vice-Mayor: SB Members: Roy Y. Salinas Generoso M. Herrera I.MariIou T. Clerigo 2.Roel M. Campos 3.Lourdes C. Mutia 4.Nanette R. Ave 5.Jaime T. Cagas 6.Jesus C. Badiang, Jr. 7.Fie1 V. culpa 8.Victor R. Torregosa, Jr. Independent Liberal Party Liberal Party Liberal Party Liberal Party Liberal Party Liberal Party Liberal Party Liberal Party UNA On August 2016, Vice-Mayor Herrera died, automatically, the 1st ranking SB Member, pursuant to Section 44 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160, assumed as Vice-Mayor therefore causes the vacancy on the 8th ranking SB Member, hence, the following queries, to wit: I. VVho will recommend and/or endorse to the appointing authority to fill-up the vacant position? Will it be the Sangguniang Bayan or the Political Party?

2. Who caused the vacancy in the Sangguniang Bayan and what Political Party should nominate following Sec. 45 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160)? 3. Whether or not the appointment of Mr. Zeromy Buba is valid considering that he has no recommendation from the Mayor to the Provincial Governor? 4. Whether or not the appointment of Mr. Zeromy Buba is valid considering that he has no recommendation/nomination from party's Provincial Chairman? 5. Whether or not the appointment of Mr. Zeromy Buba is valid considering that there is no SB Resolution favorably endorsed to the Provincial Governor? 6. On the legal interpretation of the phrase "highest official of the political party" as enunciated underSec. 45(b) orthe Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) Since query numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are interrelated to each other, we deemed it proper to tackle them in one discussion only. In the landmark case of Navarro vs. Court of Appeal', the Supreme Court ruled and has explained that in case of death of the Mayor, the "last vacancy" mentioned in Section 45(b) in relation to paragraph (c) Of the Local Government Code of 1991 is neither the vacancy caused by the elevation of the Vice Mayor to the Office of the Mayor nor the vacancy left by the last ranking sanggunian member when he was elevated to the 7th ranking position, but rather it is that vacancy caused by the elevation of the Ft ranking sanggunian member to the next higher rank, i.e. the Vice Mayor, by reason of succession. The Supreme Court ratiocinated that the reason behind the right given to a political party to nominate a replacement where a permanent vacancy occurs in the sanggunian is to maintain the party representation as willed by the people in the election. This Department believes that in electoral democracy, conscientious people may choose candidates not only because of their personal attributes and qualifications but also because of their political party affiliation. Accordingly, in the Navarro case, the political party nomination should be issued by the political party of the 1st ranking sanggunian member because he was the one who caused the last vacancy in the sanggunian due to his elevation to the position of Vice- Mayor2. Applying the foregoing, your elevation to the position of Vice-Mayor gave way to the last vacancy. In short, you have caused the vacancy. Hence in this case, Section 45(b) in relation to paragraph (c) of the Local Government Code governs. Considering that you run under a political party, that is, the Liberal Party, then the appointee to the 8th ranking position should also belong to Liberal Party. G.R. No. 141307, 28 March 2001 DILG Legal Opinion No. 37, s.2015, 22 September 2015

Per Section 45(b) of the LGC, the requisites or conditions sine qua non for the appointment of a person who will fill in the vacancy are as follows: (1) nomination from the political party concerned and a (2) certificate of membership of the appointee from the highest official of the political party concerned. In this case, records show that Mr. Buba had obtained the above-mentioned requisites/conditions for appointment. Therefore, to us, the appointment of Mr. Buba is valid. Given the above discussion, it necessarily follows then that, query numbers 3, 4 and 5 should be answered in the negative. On the other hand, we understand your concern about the status of Mr. Buba's membership in the Liberal Party, however, we would like to emphasize that we may have the authority to render opinion based on the documents submitted to us but we are not in the position to determine the legality/propriety ofthese documents. Hence, said documents are presumed valid. Finally, with respect to your number 6 query, this Department believes that the phrase "highest official of the political party" is the highest official as indicated/shown in the political party's Constitution and By-laws (i.e., the President of the Political Party). This interpretation, however, shall be without prejudice to the opinion that will be rendered by the Political Party itself. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary CC: RD Artemio B. Caneja Regional Director DILG-Region VIII LS:90
